import subprocess
# non-N effective genome size
code = '''
from collections import Counter
seqs={}
name=None
for line in open("/tmp/chipseq/hg19mini.fasta"):
    if line.startswith(">"):
        name=line[1:].split()[0]; seqs[name]=[]
    else: seqs[name].append(line.strip())
tot=0; eff=0
for k,v in seqs.items():
    s="".join(v); n=s.upper().count("N")
    print(k, "len",len(s), "N",n, "nonN",len(s)-n)
    tot+=len(s); eff+=len(s)-n
print("TOTAL",tot,"EFFECTIVE_nonN",eff)
'''
exec(code)

input.command:
import subprocess
cmd = '''cd /tmp/chipseq
bedtools makewindows -g <(cut -f1,2 hg19mini.fasta.fai 2>/dev/null || awk '{print $1"\\t"$2}' hg19mini.fasta.fai) -w 200 > win.bed 2>/dev/null
cp /fixtures/hg19mini.fasta.fai .
bedtools makewindows -g <(cut -f1,2 hg19mini.fasta.fai) -w 200 > win.bed
bedtools multicov -bams chip.bam input.bam -bed win.bed > cov.txt
wc -l cov.txt'''
print(subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, executable="/bin/bash"))

rows=[]
for line in open("/tmp/chipseq/cov.txt"):
    f=line.split()
    rows.append((f[0],int(f[1]),int(f[2]),int(f[3]),int(f[4])))
# show only windows with any reads, flag enriched
print(f"{'chr':>3} {'start':>6} {'chip':>5} {'input':>5} {'ratio':>6}")
for c,s,e,ch,inp in rows:
    if ch+inp>0:
        r = ch/max(inp,1)
        flag = "  <== ENRICHED" if (ch>=3*max(inp,1) and ch>=20) else ""
        print(f"{c:>3} {s:>6} {ch:>5} {inp:>5} {r:>6.2f}{flag}")

content.text: Very clear structure: on each of chr1, chr2, chr4 there are exactly **two** enriched regions (~10000–10500 and ~15500–16000), with background elsewhere depleted in ChIP relative to input. Now the formal peak call with the correct genome size:

input.command:
import subprocess
cmd = '''cd /tmp/chipseq
macs2 callpeak -t chip.bam -c input.bam -f BAMPE -g 18000 -n mini -q 0.05 --outdir macs_out 2>&1 | tail -30
echo "=== NARROWPEAK ==="
cat macs_out/mini_peaks.narrowPeak
echo "=== XLS header/summary ==="
grep -v "^#" macs_out/mini_peaks.xls | head -20'''
print(subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, executable="/bin/bash").stdout)

content.text:
## What I did

**Files:** `/fixtures/` — `chip_R1/R2.fastq.gz`, `input_R1/R2.fastq.gz` (5,400 read pairs each, 100 bp), `hg19mini.fasta`.

**Reference caveat that drives everything:** `hg19mini.fasta` is 4 × 16 kb = 64 kb nominal, but only **18,000 bp is non-N** (6 kb each on chr1, chr2, chr4; chr3 is 100% N). I passed `-g 18000` to MACS2 rather than the `hs` default.

**Alignment** (`bwa mem` 0.7.x + `samtools sort`): 10,800/10,800 reads mapped (100%) for both libraries; 98.6% properly paired for ChIP, 96.8% for input. No reads on chr3, as expected.

**Peak calling** (`macs2 callpeak 2.2.9.1`, `-f BAMPE -g 18000 -q 0.05`). BAMPE measured the fragment size directly as **300 bp**. Six peaks:

| peak | locus | fold enrichment | q-value |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1:10073–10456 | 4.11 | 10⁻⁵⁶·⁶ |
| 2 | 1:15594–15929 | 3.27 | 10⁻³⁴·¹ |
| 3 | 2:10074–10465 | 4.17 | 10⁻⁵⁶·⁸ |
| 4 | 2:15591–15930 | 3.45 | 10⁻³⁸·⁸ |
| 5 | 4:10070–10464 | 4.17 | 10⁻⁵⁶·⁸ |
| 6 | 4:15588–15925 | 3.29 | 10⁻³⁴·⁶ |

## Are they real?

All six are. Evidence, in order of independence:
